thought.text: The 500 is due to the placeholder project file. Let me verify the auth flow itself works.

reasoning_content:
500 on qgis with auth. Let me check the qgis-auth endpoint. The forward_auth calls nginx /api/v1/auth/qgis-auth/. Let me check backend logs.

Actually the expected behavior: qgis-auth endpoint returns 401 without auth (we saw that earlier). With basic auth it goes to qgis-server with a MAP pointing to test-project.qgz which is a fake 16-byte file. So 500 may be expected due to invalid project file. Let me test without MAP.

Actually the guide says QGIS Server: https://qgis.localhost/ows/?MAP=/projects/<project>.qgs. Since projects dir only has an empty test-project.qgz, QGIS can't render a real project. The 500 is due to the missing/invalid project. That's user-supplied data.

Let me verify the forward_auth returns 200 for authenticated. Let me test the qgis-auth directly through nginx with basic auth.

action.command:
CADDY_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' qonnectra_caddy_dev)
echo "=== qgis-auth via api (basic auth) ==="
docker run --rm --network qonnectra_network_dev curlimages/curl:latest -sk --resolve api.localhost:443:$CADDY_IP -u "admin:AdminLocalPassw0rd!" -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://api.localhost/api/v1/auth/qgis-auth/
echo "=== qgis getcapabilities (no MAP) with auth ==="
docker run --rm --network qonnectra_network_dev curlimages/curl:latest -sk --resolve qgis.localhost:443:$CADDY_IP -u "admin:AdminLocalPassw0rd!" "https://qgis.localhost/ows/?SERVICE=WMS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities" -w "\nHTTP=%{http_code}\n" | head -c 400
